# Tests s3t is expected to fail — the conformance gate.
#
# s3t runs the whole ported suite on every pull request and fails if anything
# outside this file fails, or if anything inside it passes. The list can
# therefore only shrink: a newly passing test shows up on the pull request that
# made it pass, and a newly failing one is never silently absorbed.
#
# Read it inverted: everything not listed here passes. 104 of the
# 431 tests s3t currently ports are listed.
#
# When a change makes a test pass, delete its line in the same change. CI names
# the lines to delete. Do not add lines to make CI green: a new line is a
# regression someone is choosing to keep, and it needs a reason beside it.

# --- Full ACL grammar and bucket-level ?acl (32) ------------------------------
#
# PUT ?acl reduces an AccessControlPolicy body to the nearest canned level, so
# grants to specific users are accepted and ignored, and bucket-level ?acl is
# NotImplemented outright. The access matrix these tests walk does not hold.
# Out of scope (#130): per-credential grants cover the need this server has.

# --- AWS Signature V2 (13) ----------------------------------------------------
#
# Signed with SigV2, which this server does not implement and does not plan to:
# AWS deprecated it in 2014 and refuses it for buckets created after June 2020.
# Each fails at signature verification before reaching the specific error it
# asserts. Planned and rejected in #245, with the reasoning recorded there.

# --- Expect header handling (2) -----------------------------------------------
#
# A request carrying an Expect value we do not recognise is refused 417, where S3
# ignores it and processes the request. A real gap and a small one — worth fixing
# rather than keeping, and listed here only so the gate is honest meanwhile.

s3tests/functional/test_headers.py::test_bucket_create_bad_expect_mismatch
s3tests/functional/test_headers.py::test_object_create_bad_expect_mismatch
